SCHEME FAMILY: KYLE SHANAHAN'S WIDE ZONE FAMILY [ID: shanahan-wide-zone]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Kyle Shanahan
Organization / Team: San Francisco 49ers
Category: OFFENSE
Tree Branch: shanahan-kubiak
Core Philosophy: The premier modern NFL offensive system built on horizontal stretch sequencing. The base Outside Zone run and its three constraint counters (Play-Action Deep Over, Naked Bootleg, and Jet Motion) present an identical visual picture to the defense for the first ~1.2 seconds, forcing defenders into impossible run-pass conflicts.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Outside Zone Left (ID: outside-zone)
    Personnel: 21
    Formation: Offset I, Wing Right
    Situation: 1st & 10, +40, base down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=shanahan-wide-zone&play=outside-zone

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Stretch the defense horizontally from sideline to sideline to create wide running lanes and force linebackers into overpursuit.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Mike Linebacker (Playside Flow LB)
    - Why It Works: Synchronized lateral steps by all five linemen create multiple double-teams and reach blocks; the running back tracks wide until a natural cutback crease opens.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Playside defensive end penetrating the C-gap or backside defensive tackle beating the reach block before the handoff mesh develops.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: play-action-over, naked-bootleg, jet-motion-oz
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: Base run action with full offensive line reach-and-seal flow and RB pressing the playside tackle landmark.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.5s] 1. The Lateral Reach Step: The entire offensive line fires synchronously on 45-degree lateral reach tracks toward the left sideline. The running back crosses over, aiming for the outside hip of the playside tackle.
      * [T=1.2s] 2. The Mike Linebacker Flow: The defense is forced to move horizontally. Mike linebacker triggers hard playside to protect the C-gap, creating horizontal stretch and opening cutback lanes between the linemen.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. The Three-Way Read (Bounce / Bang / Bend): The running back presses the tight tackle landmark. Seeing the edge sealed and the Mike flowing wide, the back plants his outside foot and bends sharply into the alley.
      * [T=3.5s] 4. Second-Level Cutback Burst: With backside pursuit sealed off and the Mike overrun, the back bursts through the second level into open field for an explosive gain.

>>> PLAY: Wide Zone Play-Action Deep Over (ID: play-action-over)
    Personnel: 21
    Formation: Offset I, Wing Right
    Situation: 2nd & 2, +45, shot down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.5s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=shanahan-wide-zone&play=play-action-over

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Exploit second-level defenders overplaying the run by throwing deep intermediate passes into the vacated zone behind them.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Mike Linebacker (Playside Flow LB)
    - Why It Works: Because outside zone forces the Mike to sprint laterally and downhill to protect the edge, play-action easily draws him out of intermediate pass coverage windows.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Pass rush pressure beating the line before the deep crossing route has time to clear the linebackers at 16+ yards.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: naked-bootleg
    - Plays Off: outside-zone
    - Visual Tell Cue: Backside WR (Z) cuts across the formation behind linebackers on a deep Over route instead of stalking downfield.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.5s] 1. Identical Run-Action Picture: The entire offensive line and running back mirror Outside Zone Left with 100% fidelity. For the first second, the defense sees only base run flow.
      * [T=1.2s] 2. The Linebacker Run Bite: Having been conditioned by wide zone, the Mike and Will linebackers trigger downhill into the A/B gaps to stop the run, completely abandoning intermediate zone depth.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. The Intermediate Honey Hole Opens: The QB pulls the ball at mesh. The X post route occupies the free safety deep, creating a 20-yard vacant void between the biting linebackers and the retreating deep third.
      * [T=3.5s] 4. Deep Strike Across the Formation: Z crosses cleanly behind the compromised linebackers, catching the ball in full stride with zero defenders within 10 yards.

>>> PLAY: Wide Zone Naked Bootleg (ID: naked-bootleg)
    Personnel: 21
    Formation: Offset I, Wing Right
    Situation: 1st & 10, +30, red zone boundary
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.5s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=shanahan-wide-zone&play=naked-bootleg

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Punish aggressive backside defensive ends and pursuit defenders who crash down the line against wide zone runs.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Backside Defensive End (Contain) & Strong Safety
    - Why It Works: Wide zone forces the entire defense to sprint laterally in one direction; pulling the ball and booting opposite creates a numbers advantage with no pass rushers in front of the QB.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A disciplined backside DE staying home in contain and hitting the quarterback as soon as he turns around on the bootleg.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: jet-motion-oz
    - Plays Off: outside-zone, play-action-over
    - Visual Tell Cue: QB pulls the ball out of the mesh and rolls right away from the offensive line flow, while TE releases into the backside flat.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.5s] 1. Full Wide Zone Flow Left: Offensive line and running back sprint on outside zone left tracks. The defense shifts its entire momentum to the left sideline.
      * [T=1.2s] 2. The Backside DE Crashes Inside: Strongside DE (backside contain) bites inside on the run mesh, leaving the entire right flank completely unprotected.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. QB Naked Rollout & Triangle Flood: The QB pulls the ball and sprints into open space. TE slips into the flat (short), X crosses on a drag (intermediate), and Z clears the corner (deep).
      * [T=3.4s] 4. Pitch-and-Catch in the Flat: With the defense completely out of position on the opposite hash, QB delivers an easy completion to the TE for a 15+ yard walk-in gain.

>>> PLAY: Jet Motion Outside Zone Left (ID: jet-motion-oz)
    Personnel: 21
    Formation: Offset I, Jet Motion
    Situation: 3rd & 2, +25, short yardage
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=shanahan-wide-zone&play=jet-motion-oz

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Force the defense to shift gap fits and rotate secondary coverage laterally before/at snap, creating perimeter numbers advantages.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Overhang / Strong Safety & Playside Cornerback
    - Why It Works: Jet motion pulls the cornerback wide and forces safety rotation, while the wide zone offensive line track washes the interior defensive front.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A blitzing nickel or safety shooting into the backfield to blow up the double-mesh timing before the handoff.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: None
    - Plays Off: outside-zone
    - Visual Tell Cue: Z-receiver runs full-speed jet motion across the formation before/at snap, creating a 2nd mesh point in the backfield.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.6s] 1. Jet Motion Forces Defense to Declare: Z-receiver runs full sprint across the backfield. The defense is forced to rotate safeties and bump linebackers laterally before the snap, compromising their gap integrity.
      * [T=1.2s] 2. The Double-Mesh Sequencing: The QB executes a quick jet fake to Z before handing off to the RB on wide zone. This hesitation completely freezes the Mike and holds the defensive end.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. Perimeter Overload & Crack Block: Because jet motion widened the cornerback, the X receiver easily executes an inside crack block on the Will linebacker, creating a massive perimeter highway.
      * [T=3.5s] 4. Explosive Edge Gain: The running back bounces untouched around the perimeter for a dominant chunk gain.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEME FAMILY: KLINT KUBIAK'S MOTION & SPLIT-ZONE / LEAK FAMILY [ID: kubiak-split-zone]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Klint Kubiak
Organization / Team: Las Vegas Raiders
Category: OFFENSE
Tree Branch: shanahan-kubiak
Core Philosophy: A masterclass in modern Shanahan-Kubiak sequencing. By marrying heavy 12-personnel condensed formations, pre-snap glide/orbit motion, and under-center split-zone run mechanics, Kubiak presents an identical visual picture before unleashing devastating intermediate Dagger shots, explosive backside Y-Leaks, and rapid perimeter tosses.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Split Zone (Slice) (ID: split-zone-slice)
    Personnel: 12
    Formation: 12P Condensed Wing Right
    Situation: 1st & 10, +45, base down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (Single-High) (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=kubiak-split-zone&play=split-zone-slice

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Use split-flow action to punish aggressive horizontal pursuit and create a massive cutback alley behind a sealing H-back.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Backside Defensive End (WDE) & Mike Linebacker
    - Why It Works: Offensive line stretch forces the front to flow laterally while the H-back slices across the grain to kick out the unblocked backside edge. Linebackers flowing with the line are sealed off, opening an explosive backside cutback crease.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A disciplined backside DE squeezing down the line to spill the H-back block, or interior DT penetration blowing up the mesh.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: pa-dagger-shot, boot-throwback-leak, orbit-motion-toss
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: Base foundation call: H-Back slices across the formation to kick out the backside DE on true zone run.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Condensed 12P Alignment & Tight Splits: Kubiak lines up in a condensed 12 personnel wing set. Tight WR splits compress the defensive front, creating favorable blocking angles on the perimeter.
      * [T=0.6s] The Lateral Stretch & Split Flow: The offensive line surges laterally to the right in zone synchronization. Simultaneously, H-Back (H) slices back across the grain, leaving backside WDE unblocked by design.
      * [T=1.2s] Linebackers Commit to Run Flow: The lateral stretch sucks Mike and Will linebackers hard toward the strongside B-gap, opening a massive natural cutback void behind them.
      * [T=1.8s] The H-Back Slice Kickout & RB Cutback: H delivers a crushing kickout block on the crashing WDE. The RB plants his playside foot, bends back against the grain, and explodes through the split-zone alley.
      * [T=3.4s] Second-Level Explosion: With the climbing Center pinning Mike and LT walling off Will, the RB bursts untouched into the secondary for an explosive chunk gain.

>>> PLAY: Play-Action Dagger Shot (ID: pa-dagger-shot)
    Personnel: 12
    Formation: 12P Condensed Wing Right
    Situation: 2nd & 2, +40, run-heavy down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (Single-High) (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.5s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=kubiak-split-zone&play=pa-dagger-shot

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Exploit aggressive linebacker run fits by pairing a hard split-zone play-action fake with a clear-out post and intermediate Dagger (dig) route.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Mike Linebacker & Single-High Free Safety (FS)
    - Why It Works: The split-zone mesh pulls linebackers 5-8 yards downhill toward the line of scrimmage, while the tight end clear-out post occupies the single-high safety deep. The Dagger route breaks into the wide open intermediate void between the two levels.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A disciplined Mike LB dropping under the dig route, or immediate edge pressure beating the play-action protection.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: boot-throwback-leak
    - Plays Off: split-zone-slice
    - Visual Tell Cue: Backside X stems vertical into intermediate Dagger instead of stalk blocking; QB pulls ball at t=1.3s.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Identical Condensed Split-Zone Look: Offense shows the exact same 12-personnel condensed formation and under-center posture that established the base Split-Zone run.
      * [T=0.6s] The Deceptive Split-Zone Mesh: Offensive line sells lateral stretch right while H-Back slices across. Mike and Will linebackers sprint downhill into the line to plug the run.
      * [T=1.3s] The Linebacker Trap & Play-Action Pull: QB violently pulls the ball at t=1.3s and steps into a deep 5-step pocket. The linebackers are trapped 10 yards out of position near the line of scrimmage.
      * [T=2.7s] The Clear-Out Post Drags the Deep Safety: Inline TE stems vertical on a deep post, turning the single-high Free Safety away from the middle of the field and opening a massive intermediate passing window.
      * [T=3.6s] The Dagger Strike into the Void: Backside X snaps off a crisp 15-yard Dagger right behind the stranded linebackers and underneath the cleared-out safety for an explosive 25-yard gain.

>>> PLAY: Boot Throwback Y-Leak (ID: boot-throwback-leak)
    Personnel: 12
    Formation: 12P Condensed Wing Right
    Situation: 1st & 10, +30, red zone boundary shot
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (Single-High) (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.8s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=kubiak-split-zone&play=boot-throwback-leak

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Devastate over-aggressive defenses with the signature Y-Leak constraint: faking a slice block before leaking the H-back vertically into vacated boundary space.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Backside Defensive End (WDE) & Boundary Cornerback (LCB)
    - Why It Works: The split-zone fake pulls the entire front seven and strong safety to the right. X’s deep post route drags the boundary corner inside, leaving the entire left sideline completely abandoned for the leaking H-back.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A disciplined backside DE or safety staying in deep boundary discipline and not biting on the run/post action.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: orbit-motion-toss
    - Plays Off: split-zone-slice, pa-dagger-shot
    - Visual Tell Cue: H-Back bluffs the kick-out block on backside DE and leaks vertically untouched down the sideline.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Condensed Split-Zone Pre-Snap Look: Identical 12P condensed wing alignment. Defense expects another heavy dose of inside/split-zone running.
      * [T=0.6s] Full Zone Stretch & Slice Action: Offensive line sells lateral stretch right. H-Back slices across the formation, heading straight for the unblocked backside WDE.
      * [T=1.2s] The Bluff Block at the Line of Scrimmage: H makes subtle bluff contact with WDE at the line of scrimmage to simulate the kickout block, while QB executes a naked bootleg rollout to the left.
      * [T=2.4s] The Stealth Y-Leak Slip: While the entire defense flows right or chases the QB, H slips completely untouched through the line and accelerates vertically up the left sideline.
      * [T=3.8s] The Throwback Strike for the Touchdown: With boundary corner LCB cleared out by X and safety FS pinned inside, QB squares up and throws back across the grain to H for a walk-in explosive score.

>>> PLAY: Orbit Motion Perimeter Toss (ID: orbit-motion-toss)
    Personnel: 12
    Formation: 12P Condensed Wing Right (Orbit Motion)
    Situation: 3rd & 1, +35, high-leverage perimeter call
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (Single-High) (4-3 Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=kubiak-split-zone&play=orbit-motion-toss

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Outflank aggressive defenses by combining pre-snap orbit motion and a rapid perimeter toss with multiple pulling lead blockers.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Strong Safety (SS) & Strongside Defensive End (SDE)
    - Why It Works: Pre-snap orbit motion distorts secondary coverage leverage. The quick toss gets the ball past the line of scrimmage in ~1.0s, allowing the pulling H-back and motion receiver to overwhelm edge run support.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A fast-flowing nickel/overhang shooting the backfield gap, or defensive line penetration disrupting the toss.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: split-zone-slice
    - Plays Off: split-zone-slice
    - Visual Tell Cue: Z runs pre-snap orbit motion behind the QB to distort secondary fits before snap.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Fast Orbit Motion & Formation Distortion: Speedy Z receiver sweeps in fast orbit motion behind the QB right at snap, pulling secondary eyes and creating immediate +1 numerical leverage to the perimeter.
      * [T=1.0s] The Quick Perimeter Pitch & Toss: QB executes a quick reverse pivot and pitches the ball out to the sprinting RB, getting the ball to the edge faster than the front seven can scrape.
      * [T=1.8s] The H-Back Lead & Crack Block Combo: H pulls around the tight end and destroys SS in the alley, while the motion receiver Z cracks down on RCB to create a massive sideline runway.
      * [T=2.6s] Turning the Corner into Green Grass: RB follows the lead escort past the numbers, turning the corner into open space with only the deep safety left to pursue.
      * [T=4.2s] Explosive Perimeter Chunk: RB bursts 15+ yards down the sideline, punishing defenses trying to overplay Kubiak’s inside split-zone actions.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEME FAMILY: ANDY REID'S SPREAD-RPO & MESH PASSING FAMILY [ID: reid-spread-rpo]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Andy Reid
Organization / Team: Kansas City Chiefs
Category: OFFENSE
Tree Branch: reid-west-coast
Core Philosophy: The pinnacle of modern hybrid football. Andy Reid synthesizes classic West Coast horizontal passing and timed rhythm with modern spread RPO tags, Mesh shallow crossing rub combinations, misdirection power shovel passes, and perimeter sprintout smash-wheel concepts. Operating out of 11-personnel Gun Trips alignments, Reid stresses second-level conflict defenders with identical pre-snap looks before unleashing lethal horizontal and vertical route combinations.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Mesh Shallow Cross (ID: mesh-shallow-cross)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: 11P Gun Trips Right
    Situation: 2nd & 6, +35, boundary hash
    Defensive Look: Cover 2 / Quarters MOFO (Nickel 4-2-5 Over Front)
    Animation Duration: 4.5s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=reid-spread-rpo&play=mesh-shallow-cross

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Create impossible natural pick/rub traffic for underneath zone and man defenders while stretching the defense horizontally and vertically with perimeter rail and deep clearout routes.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Mike Linebacker & Nickel DB (Underneath Hook/Curl defenders)
    - Why It Works: By crossing H and Y at 5-6 yards depth within arm's reach, underneath defenders cannot switch or track across the formation without colliding, freeing H for an easy catch in stride with massive YAC potential.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Underneath defenders passing off the crossers cleanly with banjo calls, or interior defensive tackle quick pressure collapsing the pocket before the mesh crosses.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: rpo-glance-post, power-shovel-option, sprintout-smash-wheel
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: Base mesh timing with RB releasing on a wide rail route while slot receivers execute underneath shallow cross rub.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Pre-Snap Trips Right Alignment & MOFO Shell: Andy Reid aligns in 11 Personnel Gun Trips Right. The defense shows a two-high Middle of Field Open (MOFO) shell, creating space for underneath horizontal crossers.
      * [T=1.0s] The Mesh Release & Initial Route Stems: H and Y release on crossing paths at 5 and 6 yards depth, aiming for an arm-to-arm high-five rub. RB releases on a rapid rail route to widen the boundary Will linebacker.
      * [T=1.8s] Underneath Rub Conflict on Mike & Nickel: As H crosses underneath Y, the Nickel defender is impeded by the crossing body. The Mike is frozen in space, unable to pass off or mirror H through the collision traffic.
      * [T=2.6s] Mesh Separation & RB Rail Isolation: H clears the rub with clear green grass in the boundary flat. With the Will linebacker pulled wide by the RB rail route, the underneath throwing lane is completely open.
      * [T=3.8s] Open Crosser Catch & Run-After-Catch (YAC): The QB delivers a strike in stride to H at the boundary hash, allowing Travis Kelce to turn upfield into open space for an explosive chunk gain.

>>> PLAY: Inside Zone RPO Glance (ID: rpo-glance-post)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: 11P Gun Trips Right
    Situation: 1st & 10, +42, open field
    Defensive Look: Quarters / Cover 4 Match (Nickel 4-2-5 Over Front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=reid-spread-rpo&play=rpo-glance-post

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Put the backside second-level linebacker in an inescapable run-pass conflict, punishing aggressive run fits with immediate intermediate completions.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Will Linebacker (Backside Run-Fit Conflict Defender)
    - Why It Works: Inside zone action forces Will LB to trigger into the B-gap. Because the cornerback is in off-coverage, X's sharp glance cut attacks the exact window Will vacated, giving the QB a wide-open throw before the safety can trigger.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Will LB buzzing out into the throwing lane under the glance, or boundary safety driving downhill aggressively on the slant stem.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: power-shovel-option
    - Plays Off: mesh-shallow-cross
    - Visual Tell Cue: QB reads backside Will linebacker crashing the B-gap and pulls ball for rapid glance release to X.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 11P Trips Right Alignment & Pre-Snap Conflict Read: Reid shows the identical 11 Personnel Gun Trips Right formation. The QB identifies the backside Will linebacker as the key conflict defender in Quarters coverage.
      * [T=0.8s] Inside Zone Mesh Fake & Linebacker Downhill Trigger: The offensive line surges left on an inside zone track. The QB rides the mesh with the RB, forcing the Will linebacker to crash into the B-gap to fit the run.
      * [T=1.4s] QB Pull & Rapid Second-Level Window Vacated: With the Will linebacker sucked into the line of scrimmage, the QB cleanly pulls the ball from the mesh. A massive intermediate passing window opens directly behind the linebacker.
      * [T=2.2s] Glance Delivery Behind Crashing Will LB: X breaks sharply on his 5-step glance route at 45 degrees, cutting inside the cushion of the off-cornerback. The QB fires a laser into the vacated window.
      * [T=3.2s] X Receives in Stride for Explosive YAC: X catches the pass in full stride between the hashes, easily beating the trailing cornerback and splitting the deep safeties for a huge explosive play.

>>> PLAY: Power Shovel Option (ID: power-shovel-option)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: 11P Gun Trips Right
    Situation: 3rd & 3, +18, red zone
    Defensive Look: Cover 2 Man / Match (Nickel 4-2-5 Over Front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=reid-spread-rpo&play=power-shovel-option

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Create an unstoppable misdirection interior shovel pass that exploits defensive ends widening to defend the quarterback perimeter option and sweep threat.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Strongside Defensive End (SDE) & Mike Linebacker
    - Why It Works: Guard pulling right and QB sprinting toward the sideline forces the edge defenders and linebackers to scrape wide; H slips underneath against the grain directly into the vacated interior tunnel for an easy forward completion and huge lane.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Defensive tackle penetrating into the backfield to disrupt the shovel toss path, or a disciplined interior linebacker refusing to bite on the perimeter action.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: None
    - Plays Off: mesh-shallow-cross, rpo-glance-post
    - Visual Tell Cue: Offensive guard pulls frontside while QB executes forward shovel option to TE inserting through A-gap.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Gun Trips Right Alignment & Shovel Motion Cue: Andy Reid lines up in his signature 11P Trips look in the high red zone. H (Travis Kelce) aligns tight in the slot, prepared to slice back inside.
      * [T=0.7s] Frontside Guard Power Pull & Perimeter Option Threat: LG pulls fast on a Power track to the right. The QB sprints toward the sideline with the RB on an option pitch track, pulling SDE and Nickel DB wide.
      * [T=1.4s] Shovel Flip into the Interior Tunnel: As the defensive end widens to contain the QB, a massive tunnel opens in the A/B-gap. Kelce slips underneath and the QB flips a soft forward shovel pass into his hands in full stride.
      * [T=2.2s] H Accelerates Behind Pulling Lead Block: Kelce secures the forward pass and accelerates vertically directly behind the pulling LG, who delivers a crushing kickout block on the Mike linebacker.
      * [T=3.5s] Chunk Gain into the Red Zone Secondary: With the frontside sealed and second-level linebackers washed wide by the option flow, Kelce powers untouched into the secondary for a first down and goal.

>>> PLAY: Sprintout Smash-Wheel (ID: sprintout-smash-wheel)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: 11P Gun Trips Right
    Situation: 3rd & 7, +28, scoring territory
    Defensive Look: Cover 2 Invert / Palms (Nickel 4-2-5 Over Front)
    Animation Duration: 4.4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=reid-spread-rpo&play=sprintout-smash-wheel

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Outflank perimeter pass rush with a moving pocket sprintout while executing a smash-wheel concept that punishes squatting Cover 2 cornerbacks.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Right Cornerback (RCB) & Strong Safety (SS)
    - Why It Works: Sprintout rollout cuts the throwing distance to the sideline in half. When the outside cornerback bites downhill on the inside slot hitch, Z blows past him on the wheel route into the massive void along the sideline before the deep safety can rotate over.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Strong safety reading the wheel immediately and taking a sharp downhill angle, or edge rusher blowing past the tackle to sack the QB before he reaches the launch perimeter.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: None
    - Plays Off: mesh-shallow-cross
    - Visual Tell Cue: QB takes half-roll sprintout launch point to perimeter while outside receiver runs high-speed smash-wheel.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 11P Trips Right Alignment & Perimeter Overload: Reid shows the same 11 Personnel Trips Right formation. The defense sits in a two-high Cover 2 / Palms shell, aiming to aggressively defend the sticks.
      * [T=0.8s] Half-Roll Sprintout Action & Launch Point Shift: The QB sprints out to the right with the RB securing the perimeter edge. By moving the pocket outside the tackle box, Reid changes the launch angle and shortens the sideline throw.
      * [T=1.6s] Corner Squats on Underneath Hitch: H snaps off a crisp 5-yard hitch route. The field cornerback (RCB) aggressively bites downhill to tackle the hitch at the sticks, falling directly into the Smash-Wheel trap.
      * [T=2.5s] Z Accelerates Down Sideline on Wheel Route: Having faked an inside slant stem, Z plants his foot and bursts vertically down the sideline on the wheel. With Y holding the deep safety inside, Z flies into open space.
      * [T=3.4s] Deep Hole-Shot Delivery Over the Squatted Corner: The QB uncorks a pinpoint hole shot over the squatted corner and away from the recovering safety, dropping the ball into Z’s hands for a 28-yard touchdown strike.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEME FAMILY: SEAN MCVAY'S CONDENSED DUO & PLAY-ACTION ATTACK [ID: mcvay-duo-playaction]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Sean McVay
Organization / Team: Los Angeles Rams
Category: OFFENSE
Tree Branch: shanahan-kubiak
Core Philosophy: Sean McVay's championship offensive system engineered around condensed 11-personnel formations with tight receiver splits. By pairing physical 'Power without a puller' Duo double-teams with identical play-action 3-level Sail floods, explosive deep crossing over-routes, and rapid Glance RPOs, McVay keeps defensive front sevens in permanent schematic conflict.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: 11P Duo Lead Inside Power Run (ID: mcvay-duo-lead-run)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: 11P Condensed Bunch Right
    Situation: 1st & 10, +45, early down base
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Match (4-2-5 Nickel Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=mcvay-duo-playaction&play=mcvay-duo-lead-run

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Punish light nickel boxes with vertical double-teams ("Duo"), creating massive interior movement and establishing the physical run picture that unlocks play-action shot plays.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Mike Linebacker (Playside Interior LB)
    - Why It Works: Dual simultaneous double-teams generate relentless vertical push; the running back presses frontside until the Mike commits, then cuts back behind the Center’s interior seal.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A dominant 3-tech DT splitting the RG/RT double-team or safety flying down unblocked into the cutback alley before the RB can press the line.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: mcvay-pa-sail-flood, mcvay-pa-deep-crosser, mcvay-glance-rpo-orbit
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: Offensive line vertical-punch double teams climbing to Mike linebacker; no pulling guard, RB presses interior A-gap mesh.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.6s] 1. Dual Interior Double-Teams: The Center and Left Guard combo the 1-tech NT, while Right Guard and Right Tackle combo the 3-tech DT. McVay creates two 600-pound vertical displacements without using a pulling guard ("Power without a puller").
      * [T=1.4s] 2. The Mesh & Mike Conflict Read: The running back tracks downhill directly into the frontside A/B gap, pressing the line of scrimmage to freeze the Mike Linebacker. The QB fakes a weakside bootleg to hold the backside defensive end.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. The Second-Level Cutback Burst: As the Mike overcommits to plug the frontside B-gap, the running back plants his outside foot and bends sharply back into the wide crevasse behind the Center’s displacement on the NT.
      * [T=3.8s] 4. Explosive Open-Field YAC: Slot receiver H pins the Nickel defender with a vicious crack block while the RB bursts through the secondary past the diving Will linebacker for an explosive 15-yard gain.

>>> PLAY: Play-Action Sail 3-Level Flood (ID: mcvay-pa-sail-flood)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: 11P Condensed Bunch Right
    Situation: 2nd & 3, +35, play-action shot
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (4-2-5 Nickel Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.5s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=mcvay-duo-playaction&play=mcvay-pa-sail-flood

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Create a 3-level vertical flood (deep clearout, 12-yard intermediate out, 2-yard flat) off under-center Duo play-action to overload Cover 3 and Cover 4 zone defenders.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Nickel Apex Defender / Strong Safety (Curl-Flat Defender)
    - Why It Works: The vertical post by Z removes the deep corner while the RB flat route pins the overhang DB near the line of scrimmage, opening an unguardable intermediate void for H on the Sail.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Immediate edge rush beating the play-action protection before the QB can set his platform or the boundary cornerback ignoring the vertical clearout to squat on the intermediate Sail.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: mcvay-pa-deep-crosser
    - Plays Off: mcvay-duo-lead-run
    - Visual Tell Cue: Slot receiver H stems vertical before breaking 90 degrees outward on a 12-yard Sail route while QB pulls the ball out of Duo mesh.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.8s] 1. The Identical Duo Run Action: The entire offensive line and running back execute the exact physical posture of the Duo lead run. The Mike and Will linebackers bite hard downhill to plug the interior gaps.
      * [T=1.6s] 2. The Apex Defender Freeze: The QB pulls the ball out of the mesh while the RB leaks into the strongside flat. The Nickel apex defender triggers downhill on the flat threat, widening the intermediate window behind him.
      * [T=2.8s] 3. The 3-Level Flood Geometry: Z’s vertical post clears out the Cover 3 corner (RCB) deep, the RB flat route holds the Nickel short, leaving Cooper Kupp (H) running wide open on the 13-yard Sail into 20 yards of empty sideline green.
      * [T=3.6s] 4. Pinpoint Strike to the Boundary: The QB sets his platform and drives a 14-yard laser into the chest of H before the strong safety can recover, creating a clean catch and 10+ yards of run-after-catch down the sideline.

>>> PLAY: Play-Action Deep Over / Crosser (ID: mcvay-pa-deep-crosser)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: 11P Condensed Bunch Right
    Situation: 1st & 10, +48, explosive shot play
    Defensive Look: Cover 4 Quarters / Match (4-2-5 Nickel Over front)
    Animation Duration: 4.5s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=mcvay-duo-playaction&play=mcvay-pa-deep-crosser

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Attack the vulnerable intermediate middle-of-the-field void (18-22 yards) against two-high and single-high defenses by pairing a deep post clearout with a crossing over-route.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Weak Safety (FS in Quarters) & Mike Linebacker
    - Why It Works: The Duo run fake pulls the Mike linebacker into the line of scrimmage, while the Z vertical post forces both deep field safeties back, leaving X in single-coverage space on an over-route with a 20-yard running start.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Free safety sitting disciplined in the deep intermediate hole rather than biting on the run fake, or backside edge rusher beating the LT before the 7-step play-action drop develops.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: mcvay-glance-rpo-orbit
    - Plays Off: mcvay-duo-lead-run, mcvay-pa-sail-flood

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.8s] 1. The Heavy Duo Play-Action Suck: The offensive line surges forward with physical Duo run blocking while the QB executes a deep under-center mesh. Both the Mike and Will linebackers violently trigger into the A/B gaps.
      * [T=1.8s] 2. The Post Clearout & Crosser Stride: Z explodes on a deep vertical post, forcing the strong safety and field corner 25 yards downfield. Meanwhile, X takes a clean inside release, building full acceleration into the deep intermediate void.
      * [T=2.8s] 3. The High-Low Crosser Dilemma: Tight end Y drags across at 4 yards depth, freezing the Will LB underneath. Behind the linebackers and underneath the retreating safeties, a massive 15-yard green canyon opens for X.
      * [T=3.6s] 4. The Deep Over Cannon Strike: The QB steps into a clean pocket and launches a 25-yard strike to X in full stride across the hashes, completely outflanking the defense for a 35-yard explosive touchdown.

>>> PLAY: Glance RPO with Orbit Return Motion (ID: mcvay-glance-rpo-orbit)

    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Will Linebacker (Weakside Second-Level Conflict Defender)
    - Why It Works: Pre-snap orbit motion holds the strong safety while the Duo run mesh pulls the Will linebacker downhill, creating an uncontested throwing window on the skinny slant to X.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Will linebacker staying disciplined in the slant throwing lane while defensive front stuffs the Duo run with a light box, or quarterback misreading the conflict key and forcing a contested throw.

      * [T=1.8s] 3. The Quick Glance Strike: The QB plants and fires a quick-release dart on a 6-yard Glance slant to X, hitting him in the vacant window directly vacated by the crashing Will linebacker.
      * [T=3.2s] 4. Red Zone Touchdown Burst: X snatches the ball in stride, defeats the off-balance boundary corner, and slices between the closing safeties for an explosive 28-yard red-zone touchdown.

SCHEME FAMILY: MIKE MCDANIEL'S SPEED CHEAT-MOTION & SPACE ATTACK [ID: mcdaniel-cheat-motion]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Mike McDaniel
Organization / Team: Los Angeles Chargers
Category: OFFENSE
Tree Branch: shanahan-kubiak
Core Philosophy: Mike McDaniel's revolutionary speed-in-space scheme that weaponizes pre-snap 'Cheat Motion' (sprint-speed motion at the snap). By giving explosive playmakers a running start to crack edge defenders on perimeter tosses, feigning cracks on devastating sideline wheel shots, punishing overpursuit with inside zone Wham traps, and running pistol speed options in the red zone, McDaniel creates mathematical dilemmas for any defense.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Cheat Motion Crack Toss Perimeter Stretch (ID: mcdaniel-cheat-motion-toss)
    Personnel: 21
    Formation: 21P Gun Offset, Cheat Motion Right
    Situation: 1st & 10, +45, perimeter speed attack
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Match (4-3 Under front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=mcdaniel-cheat-motion&play=mcdaniel-cheat-motion-toss

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Weaponize extreme pre-snap speed ("Cheat Motion") to create an unmatchable angle on the perimeter, cracking the edge defender and pulling offensive linemen for an explosive outside toss.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: SAM Linebacker / Strongside Edge Defender
    - Why It Works: The receiver hits the line of scrimmage at full sprint speed before the snap, allowing a 190-pound receiver to violently pin a 245-pound linebacker who cannot see the crack coming.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Field cornerback blowing up the crack block by shooting inside immediately or running back hesitating on the toss track rather than sprinting directly to the perimeter.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: mcdaniel-cheat-motion-wheel, mcdaniel-inside-zone-wham
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: Receiver in cheat motion snaps inside to deliver crack block on edge/LB while RB takes immediate wide toss track.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.5s] 1. The Pre-Snap Cheat Motion Sprint: Z (Tyreek Hill role) explodes in full-sprint cheat motion towards the tackle box before the snap. At the snap, he is already traveling at 18 mph with unstoppable downhill momentum.
      * [T=1.2s] 2. The Devastating Crack-and-Pull: Z delivers a crushing blindside crack block on the SAM linebacker, while the Right Tackle and Fullback pull violently around the perimeter to form a two-man escort wall.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. Turning the Corner at Full Speed: The running back receives the rapid toss while already at top speed, outflanking the defense and cutting off RT’s kick-out block on the field corner into open sideline grass.
      * [T=3.5s] 4. 20+ MPH Boundary Explosion: FB erases the strong safety in the alley while the running back accelerates past 21 mph down the sideline, leaving the free safety taking an impossible pursuit angle.

>>> PLAY: Cheat Motion Wheel Shot (Speed Release) (ID: mcdaniel-cheat-motion-wheel)
    Personnel: 21
    Formation: 21P Gun Offset, Cheat Motion Right
    Situation: 2nd & 2, +38, explosive shot play
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky / Quarters Match (4-3 Under front)
    Animation Duration: 4.5s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=mcdaniel-cheat-motion&play=mcdaniel-cheat-motion-wheel

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Punish defenses over-committing to McDaniel’s Cheat Motion perimeter crack toss by bluffing the crack block and releasing the fastest receiver on an uncontested vertical wheel route.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Field Cornerback (RCB) & Strong Safety
    - Why It Works: The threat of the perimeter toss forces the cornerback and safety to trigger downhill against the run; once they lose outside leverage, no defender in football can recover against Tyreek Hill-level speed on a wheel route.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Cornerback playing deep quarters match and refusing to bite on the toss fake, or safety immediately rolling over top to double the wheel route.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: mcdaniel-pistol-option-pitch
    - Plays Off: mcdaniel-cheat-motion-toss
    - Visual Tell Cue: Motion receiver bluffs crack block for 0.4s then explosive vertical burst along the boundary on the wheel route.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.6s] 1. The Identical Cheat Motion Sprint: Z enters full-speed sprint motion, mirroring the crack toss look. The field corner (RCB) and strong safety (SS) aggressively drive downhill toward the line of scrimmage to defend the run.
      * [T=1.2s] 2. The Fake Crack & Sideline Wheel Break: Z flashes an inside stem to bluff the crack block on the SAM, then plants and violently breaks up the boundary at 22 mph on a wheel route. The entire secondary is caught flat-footed.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. Blown Coverage & Separation: TE’s intermediate crossing dig holds the single-high free safety in the center of the field, while Z blows past the recovering corner to create 8 yards of pure separation.
      * [T=3.8s] 4. The 38-Yard Deep Touchdown Bomb: The QB launches a high-arcing rainbow pass down the right numbers. Z catches the ball in stride at the 5-yard line and cruises into the end zone for an explosive touchdown.

>>> PLAY: Inside Zone Wham with Cheat Decoy (ID: mcdaniel-inside-zone-wham)
    Personnel: 21
    Formation: 21P Pistol Sniffer, Cheat Motion Left
    Situation: 1st & 10, +32, interior counter-punch
    Defensive Look: Cover 2 Quarters / Two-High Shell (4-3 Over front)

    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=mcdaniel-cheat-motion&play=mcdaniel-inside-zone-wham

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Exploit defensive lateral overpursuit with an inside zone Wham trap, using pre-snap speed motion as eye candy while trapping the 3-tech DT from the blindside.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: 3-Technique Defensive Tackle & Mike Linebacker
    - Why It Works: The 3-tech is left unblocked by design, tempting him to shoot upfield where he is blindsided by the H-back’s trap block; Meanwhile, the pre-snap motion vacates the second level.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: 3-technique DT reading the trap release and squeezing inside before the FB can deliver the Wham block, or sniffer FB whiffing on the trap collision.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: mcdaniel-pistol-option-pitch
    - Plays Off: mcdaniel-cheat-motion-toss
    - Visual Tell Cue: FB/H-back cuts back against the grain on a wham trap block on the 3T DT instead of leading to the perimeter.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.5s] 1. The Pre-Snap Cheat Motion Decoy: Z fires across the formation in full-speed cheat motion. The Will linebacker, Mike linebacker, and Free Safety all rotate aggressively left to stop the anticipated perimeter speed sweep.
      * [T=1.0s] 2. The Unblocked 3-Tech Trap: Right Guard completely bypasses the 3-technique defensive tackle, releasing directly to the second level. The 3T penetrates upfield thinking he has free penetration into the backfield.
      * [T=1.6s] 3. The Blindside Wham Collision: Sniffer fullback FB comes across against the grain and delivers a crushing Wham block on the 3T’s blindside hip, pinning him and creating a 5-yard interior highway.
      * [T=2.8s] 4. North-South A-Gap Explosion: With linebackers washed out by the motion decoy and the RG erasing the Mike, the running back hits the B-gap crease at full speed for an explosive 18-yard carry.

>>> PLAY: Pistol Speed Option Pitch & Space Read (ID: mcdaniel-pistol-option-pitch)
    Personnel: 21
    Formation: 21P Pistol Split-Flow
    Situation: 3rd & 2, +15, red zone perimeter space
    Defensive Look: Cover 1 Man / Cover 3 Match (4-3 Under front)

    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Strongside Defensive End (Option Read Key)
    - Why It Works: Leaving the defensive end unblocked allows offensive linemen to climb immediately to the second level; the QB forces the edge defender to commit before pitching to elite speed in space.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Defensive end slow-playing the option to disrupt the pitch track while scraping linebackers rally to tackle the QB before he can release the pitch.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]

      * [T=1.4s] 2. The Edge Read & Pitch Decision: SDE turns his shoulders and commits downhill to tackle the sprinting QB. The QB flips a clean option pitch into space to the sprinting RB.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. Violent Lead Block in the Alley: Fullback FB inserts into the perimeter alley and delivers a thunderous lead block on the filling strong safety, completely clearing the edge lane.
      * [T=3.5s] 4. Red Zone Pylon Touchdown Burst: The running back turns the corner at 21 mph, beating the diving free safety to the front pylon for an electrifying 15-yard red zone touchdown.

SCHEME FAMILY: KEVIN STEFANSKI'S MULTI-TE GAP & UNDER-CENTER PLAY-ACTION FAMILY [ID: stefanski-multi-te-gap]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Kevin Stefanski
Organization / Team: Atlanta Falcons
Category: OFFENSE
Tree Branch: shanahan-kubiak
Core Philosophy: Master of condensed multi-tight end structures, violent pin-and-pull gap schemes, GT counter lead concepts, and deep play-action seam/bootleg shots. Kevin Stefanski builds an overpowering offensive machine founded on angle blocking, devastating complementary under-center fakes, and high-efficiency vertical passing off run action.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: 13P Pin & Pull Sweep (ID: stefanski-pin-pull-sweep)
    Personnel: 13
    Formation: 13P Heavy Wing Right
    Situation: 1st & 10, +45, heavy run down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (Single-High) (4-3 Over Front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=stefanski-multi-te-gap&play=stefanski-pin-pull-sweep

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Create overwhelming perimeter gap leverage against single-high defenses by pinning frontside defensive linemen inside and pulling interior linemen as lead escorts.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Strong Safety (SS) & Mike Linebacker (MIKE)
    - Why It Works: Down blocks by the tackle and tight ends create natural, impenetrable blocking angles that neutralize defensive penetration. Pulling interior linemen provide massive lead blockers against smaller defensive backs in the alley.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A defensive lineman penetrating between the down blocks or a fast-flowing safety blowing up the pulling guard behind the line of scrimmage.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: stefanski-pa-seam-shot, stefanski-naked-boot-slide
    - Plays Off: stefanski-counter-gap-lead
    - Visual Tell Cue: Center & RG immediately pull playside while RT & Y down-block (pin).

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Heavy 13-Personnel Condensed Front: Stefanski aligns 3 tight ends (Inline Y, Wing F, Backside U) in a condensed wing set to create overwhelming numerical leverage at the point of attack.
      * [T=0.8s] The Pin-Down Wall & Dual Pullers: RT, Y, and F execute devastating down blocks pinning the 3T, SDE, and Sam LB inside, while Center and RG pull into the perimeter alley.
      * [T=1.8s] RG Kickout & Center Alley Wrap: RG violently kicks out Strong Safety SS on the perimeter edge, while Center wraps up into the alley to seal the scraping Mike linebacker.
      * [T=2.8s] RB Plants & Detonates Through Crease: Running back presses the perimeter toss, plants his outside foot inside the RG kickout, and accelerates 15+ yards through the gaping alley crease.

>>> PLAY: Play-Action Seam Shot (ID: stefanski-pa-seam-shot)
    Personnel: 13
    Formation: 13P Heavy Wing Right
    Situation: 2nd & 1, +42, aggressive shot down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (Single-High) (4-3 Over Front)
    Animation Duration: 4.4s

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]

    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Free Safety (FS) & Strong Safety (SS)
    - Why It Works: The single-high safety and linebackers bite hard downhill on the simulated pin-pull pull action, completely vacating the deep middle and seam areas where the tight end releases vertically with maximum speed.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A deep Free Safety who maintains discipline without biting downhill, or an immediate free edge rusher disrupting the under-center 7-step drop.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]

    - Plays Off: stefanski-pin-pull-sweep

      * [T=1.8s] The Seam Release into the Void: Y tight end flash-chips the defensive end and explodes untouched up the right seam, running into the massive intermediate void vacated by the linebackers.
      * [T=3.2s] The Deep Shot Strike: QB violently pulls the ball, sets at 7-step depth, and delivers a laser down the seam to Y for a 25-yard touchdown behind the stranded safety.

>>> PLAY: Naked Bootleg Slide (ID: stefanski-naked-boot-slide)
    Personnel: 13
    Formation: 13P Heavy Wing Right
    Situation: 2nd & 4, +32, red zone edge
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky / Flow Match (4-3 Over Front)
    Animation Duration: 4.4s

    - Why It Works: The aggressive sweep action pulls all 7 front-seven defenders flowing horizontally right. When the quarterback rolls naked left, there are literally zero defensive players left in the weakside flat.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A disciplined backside edge defender who stays home for bootleg contain, forcing the QB to throw away or take a sack.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: stefanski-counter-gap-lead
    - Plays Off: stefanski-pin-pull-sweep, stefanski-pa-seam-shot

      * [T=2.0s] The Naked Bootleg Rollout: QB executes a pristine bootleg fake, pulls the ball cleanly, and rolls naked back to the left into 20 yards of empty green grass.
      * [T=2.8s] The Slide Strike in Wide Open Space: Backside inline TE U slips underneath the crashed edge on the Slide route, catching a crisp strike on the run from QB for a 14-yard first down.

>>> PLAY: Counter Gap GT Lead (ID: stefanski-counter-gap-lead)
    Personnel: 13
    Formation: 13P Heavy Wing Right
    Situation: 3rd & 2, +28, short yardage
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Match (4-3 Over Front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=stefanski-multi-te-gap&play=stefanski-counter-gap-lead

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Gasoline the defense with heavy gap-scheme power: down blocks create an unmovable wall, while a pulling guard kicks out the edge and a lead tight end pancakes the linebacker.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Strongside Defensive End (SDE) & Mike Linebacker (MIKE)
    - Why It Works: Down blocks give offensive linemen superior angles of leverage. The pulling guard creates a massive gap by kicking the edge defender out, while the lead-blocking tight end ensures the running back enters the secondary untouched.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A penetrating defensive tackle shooting through the vacated backside guard gap or an edge defender spilling inside to blow up the pullers.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: stefanski-pin-pull-sweep
    - Plays Off: stefanski-naked-boot-slide
    - Visual Tell Cue: Backside LG and F pull across formation on GT/GF counter paths; RB takes counter jab step before cutting back.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] 13-Personnel Heavy Alignment: Stefanski shows his hallmark heavy 3-TE set, daring the defense to load the box before executing counter gap mechanics.
      * [T=0.6s] Down Blocks & Backside Pullers: RT and Y execute down blocks to seal the interior, while backside LG and Wing F pull across the formation into the attack point.
      * [T=1.8s] The Kickout & Lead Collision: LG violently kicks out the edge defender SDE, while F wraps tight through the B/C gap crease to pancake the Mike linebacker.
      * [T=2.8s] RB Gash Through the Crease: Running back follows the pulling convoy, cuts off the inside shoulder of the LG kickout, and erupts into the secondary for a 16-yard gain.

SCHEME FAMILY: SHANE STEICHEN'S QB MESH & SPREAD RPO SYSTEM [ID: steichen-qb-mesh-rpo]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Shane Steichen
Organization / Team: Indianapolis Colts
Category: OFFENSE
Tree Branch: reid-west-coast
Core Philosophy: A dual-threat quarterback maximization system rooted in Andy Reid's West Coast principles with modern college Spread DNA. Shane Steichen pairs zone-read power runs with RPO bubble/glance perimeter reads, Mesh shallow crosses that create natural rubs against man coverage, and vertical switch releases that exploit deep zone voids. The system demands a mobile signal-caller who threatens the edge on every designed run, compressing defensive end responsibilities into an impossible choice.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Gun QB Power Read (ID: steichen-qb-power-read)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: 11P Gun Spread Right
    Situation: 1st & 10, +48, open field
    Defensive Look: Nickel Cover 2 / Quarters (Nickel 4-2-5 Over Front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=steichen-qb-mesh-rpo&play=steichen-qb-power-read

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Put the frontside defensive end in an impossible spatial dilemma: if he widens to stop the perimeter sweep, the dual-threat QB powers downhill behind a pulling guard.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Strongside Defensive End (SDE) & Mike Linebacker (MIKE)
    - Why It Works: The threat of the speed sweep forces the edge defender and nickel DB to play with wide leverage, eliminating the defense's force support and creating a massive downhill power gap.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A defensive tackle who defeats the down block inside or a disciplined DE who shuffles and plays both the keep and the pitch.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: steichen-zone-bubble-rpo, steichen-verticals-switch
    - Plays Off: steichen-mesh-rail-wheel
    - Visual Tell Cue: Backside RG pulls playside while RB crosses on horizontal sweep path; QB reads frontside DE.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Spread 11-Personnel Power Read Look: Steichen spaces the defense across the width of the field in 11-personnel Gun Spread, isolating the frontside defensive end as the unblocked read defender.
      * [T=0.6s] The Jet Sweep Mesh & DE Conflict: RB crosses on a full-speed horizontal sweep track. Frontside SDE widens laterally to prevent the perimeter sweep, immediately opening the interior gap cavity.
      * [T=1.6s] The QB Keep & Pulling Guard Escort: QB reads the widening DE, firmly pulls the ball from the mesh, and explodes downhill into the B-gap behind pulling guard RG.
      * [T=2.6s] RG Decimates Mike LB in the Hole: RG violently pancakes the Mike linebacker at the line of scrimmage, allowing the QB to burst untouched into the secondary for a 15-yard gain.

>>> PLAY: Mesh Rail / Wheel (ID: steichen-mesh-rail-wheel)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: 11P Gun Spread Right
    Situation: 3rd & 5, +35, money down
    Defensive Look: Nickel Cover 1 Man / Match (Nickel 4-2-5 Over Front)
    Animation Duration: 4.5s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=steichen-qb-mesh-rpo&play=steichen-mesh-rail-wheel

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Exploit man-to-man coverage by pairing a tight shallow-cross Mesh rub with an explosive running back Rail/Wheel route along the boundary.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Will Linebacker (WILL) & Free Safety (FS)
    - Why It Works: In man coverage, the linebacker assigned to the running back must fight through the crossing receiver traffic. The Mesh concept acts as a natural legal pick, allowing the faster running back to achieve unobstructed separation down the boundary.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Zone coverage (like Cover 2 or Cover 4) where the boundary cornerback or safety is waiting in the deep half to intercept the wheel throw.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: steichen-qb-power-read
    - Plays Off: steichen-zone-bubble-rpo
    - Visual Tell Cue: RB free-releases on boundary rail/wheel route while slot receivers set tight crossing rub.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Spread 11-Personnel Mesh Alignment: Steichen aligns in 11 Gun Spread, isolating boundary matchups while preparing dual shallow crossing routes across the middle.
      * [T=0.8s] The Free-Release Rail & Mesh Rub: RB accelerates freely into the boundary flat, while TE and H execute precise crossing paths at 4 yards to create a wall of traffic in the middle of the field.
      * [T=1.8s] The Will LB Pick & Boundary Separation: Will linebacker is tasked with covering RB in man-to-man, but collides violently with the TE crosser, getting picked and trailing 4 yards behind the wheel.
      * [T=2.8s] The Teardrop Wheel Touchdown Strike: QB holds the single-high safety with his eyes, steps into a pristine pocket, and drops a 25-yard teardrop into the bucket down the boundary to RB for a touchdown.

>>> PLAY: Inside Zone + Bubble Screen RPO (ID: steichen-zone-bubble-rpo)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: 11P Gun Spread Right
    Situation: 2nd & 4, +40, tempo pace
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky / Off-Nickel (Nickel 4-2-5 Over Front)
    Animation Duration: 3.8s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=steichen-qb-mesh-rpo&play=steichen-zone-bubble-rpo

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Conflict the apex/overhang defender with a simultaneous inside zone run and perimeter bubble screen, taking whatever the defense concedes with ruthless efficiency.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Nickel DB (Overhang Conflict Key)
    - Why It Works: The defense cannot be right: if the Nickel defender fits the box to stop the inside zone, the perimeter bubble screen has a 2-on-2 numerical advantage with lead blockers. If the Nickel widens, the running back gains 6+ yards on inside zone.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A lightning-fast Nickel DB who feigns a run fit before darting outside to jump the bubble screen for a pick-six.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: steichen-verticals-switch, steichen-qb-power-read
    - Plays Off: steichen-mesh-rail-wheel
    - Visual Tell Cue: Playside WRs immediately stalk block on snap while slot WR flares on bubble arc; QB catches and throws at mesh.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Spread RPO Pre-Snap Alignment: Steichen aligns in 11 Gun Spread with a 2-man bubble screen combination to the field, putting the apex Nickel defender in direct spatial conflict.
      * [T=0.6s] The Nickel Conflict Trigger: RB attacks the A-gap on inside zone. Seeing the run look, the Nickel DB abandons his perimeter leverage and sprints downhill into the B-gap.
      * [T=1.1s] The Lightning QB Pull & Throw: QB reads the Nickel crashing, immediately pulls the ball from the mesh, and fires a lightning-fast strike to H on the perimeter bubble screen.
      * [T=2.4s] Perimeter Blocks & 14-Yard Explosive Burst: TE and Z execute textbook perimeter stalk blocks on the SS and RCB, allowing H to cut untouched up the sideline for a 14-yard gain.

>>> PLAY: 4-Verticals Switch Shot (ID: steichen-verticals-switch)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: 11P Gun Spread Right
    Situation: 1st & 10, +45, shot down
    Defensive Look: Two-High Quarters / Cover 4 (Nickel 4-2-5 Over Front)
    Animation Duration: 4.5s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=steichen-qb-mesh-rpo&play=steichen-verticals-switch

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Destroy Two-High Quarters coverage by crossing the release paths of the #1 and #2 receivers on deep vertical tracks, triggering coverage miscommunication and blown assignments.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Strong Safety (SS) & Right Cornerback (RCB)
    - Why It Works: In Quarters coverage, DBs play pattern-match rules based on receiver releases. When the outside receiver breaks inside on a post and the slot receiver wheels outside, both DBs frequently bite on the inside post, leaving the wheel vertical completely unguarded.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A safety and corner who execute seamless "switch" communication, or a 4-man defensive pass rush that gets home before the 5-step deep route develops.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: steichen-qb-power-read
    - Plays Off: steichen-zone-bubble-rpo
    - Visual Tell Cue: Slot H and outside Z cross stems at 6 yards on vertical release instead of standard screen/blocking releases.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.0s] Spread 11-Personnel Quarters Attack: Steichen dials up a deep 4-verticals switch concept against Two-High Quarters coverage, targeting the spatial rules of the field safety and cornerback.
      * [T=1.2s] The 6-Yard Stem Switch Confusion: Slot H stems inside while outside Z crosses over the top. At 6 yards, they swap vertical tracks, causing instant panic between RCB and Strong Safety SS.
      * [T=2.2s] Double-Coverage on Post Leaves Sideline Naked: Both RCB and SS squeeze inside to match Z on the post, leaving slot receiver H blowing completely uncontested down the wide open right sideline.
      * [T=3.4s] The 35-Yard Touchdown Bomb: QB steps cleanly into the pocket and delivers a breathtaking 35-yard dime to H in stride for an explosive touchdown.

SCHEME FAMILY: MATT LAFLEUR'S ILLUSION OF COMPLEXITY & DEEP SHOT FAMILY [ID: lafleur-illusion-packers]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Matt LaFleur
Organization / Team: Green Bay Packers
Category: OFFENSE
Tree Branch: shanahan-kubiak
Core Philosophy: A masterclass in schematic deception and visual illusion. Matt LaFleur marries condensed 12-personnel and dual-back Pony sets with identical under-center wide-zone run mechanics to lull defenses into overpursuing, before unlocking catastrophic deep Cross-Country Posts, Dagger intermediate concepts, and perimeter constraint wheels.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Wide Zone Cutback (Illusion Flow) (ID: lafleur-wide-zone-cutback)
    Personnel: 12
    Formation: Singleback Wing Left, Condensed Right
    Situation: 1st & 10, Own 35, base down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Match (4-3 Under Front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=lafleur-illusion-packers&play=lafleur-wide-zone-cutback

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Create wide horizontal stretch with 12-personnel under-center flow to force linebackers to overpursue and open a devastating backside cutback lane.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Mike Linebacker (Playside Flow Linebacker)
    - Why It Works: The threat of the perimeter reach forces second-level defenders to sprint horizontally; the backside boot fake freezes edge pursuit, creating a massive cutback seam.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Backside 3-technique DT shooting the B-gap immediately or playside 5-technique squeezing the reach block before the jump-cut can materialize.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: lafleur-cross-country-post, lafleur-pa-dagger-dig, lafleur-pony-screen-wheel
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: Full offensive line lateral bucket steps with under-center RB taking the handoff and pressing the tackle landmark rather than QB keeping.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.6s] 1. Synchronized Zone Reach Flow: The offensive line and playside TE fire in unison on 45-degree lateral angles. The back crosses over with rapid horizontal momentum aiming for the outside hip of the left tackle.
      * [T=1.6s] 2. The Illusory Stretch & Overpursuit: The defense reacts to the heavy 12-personnel stretch. The Mike and Will linebackers scrape hard to the boundary to avoid getting hooked, while the backside DE and SS bite on the QB’s bootleg fake.
      * [T=2.4s] 3. The Vertical Jump-Cut: With the frontside defenders hooked and the second-level linebackers overrunning their gaps, the RB plants violently off his left foot and bends back into the wide-open A/B-gap cutback lane.
      * [T=3.8s] 4. Second-Level Explosive Crease: LG and RT finish their second-level climb blocks, sealing off the linebackers and paving an explosive 10+ yard north-south gain right through the heart of the defense.

>>> PLAY: PA Cross-Country Deep Post (ID: lafleur-cross-country-post)
    Personnel: 12
    Formation: Singleback Wing Left, Condensed Right
    Situation: 2nd & 2, +45, play-action shot down
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Sky (4-3 Under Front)
    Animation Duration: 4.2s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=lafleur-illusion-packers&play=lafleur-cross-country-post

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]

    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Free Safety (Deep Middle Cover 3 Safety)
    - Why It Works: The intermediate Over route by TE1 holds the single-high safety on the right hash, allowing the backside Z receiver on a Cross-Country Post to attack the vacant deep middle/left void with maximum leverage.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Free Safety remaining disciplined in the deep middle third or an unblocked edge rusher affecting the QB before the deep 7-step play-action platform is established.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]

    - Plays Off: lafleur-wide-zone-cutback

      * [T=1.8s] 2. The Play-Action Disconnect & Over Route Release: QB executes a deep 7-step play-action drop. TE1 slips off his run fake and stems across the formation on a 12-yard intermediate Over route, drawing the eyes of both the strong safety and the deep middle free safety.
      * [T=3.0s] 3. The Cross-Country Post Break: Z receiver stems from the condensed right split, crosses the face of the right corner, and climbs across the entire formation at 22+ yards depth, slicing directly into the gaping void vacated by the lured Free Safety.
      * [T=4.2s] 4. The 45-Yard Deep Touchdown Strike: With clean 7-man protection in the pocket and X pinning the boundary corner deep, the QB launches a majestic 45-yard rainbow to Z streaking wide open across the opposite deep seam.

>>> PLAY: Pony Package Screen-Wheel Constraint (ID: lafleur-pony-screen-wheel)

    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Edge rusher RDE beating the RT quickly off the edge before the QB can pivot and reset to throw the wheel.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]

      * [T=1.8s] 2. Defensive Overpursuit & Boundary Vacuum: The defense bites hard on the screen threat: Will, Mike, LCB, and Free Safety all sprint toward the left sideline to tackle RB1 behind the line.
      * [T=2.5s] 3. The Inside-Out Wheel Release: RB2 feigns an interior lead block, then snaps violently outside the right tackle into a full-speed rail wheel down the vacated right sideline. Z’s dig route pulls the RCB inside.
      * [T=3.5s] 4. Precision Drop Down the Sideline: QB resets, squares his shoulders, and drops a 28-yard rainbow right into RB2’s breadbasket for an explosive runaway touchdown down the right sideline.

>>> PLAY: PA Dagger Seam-Dig Concept (ID: lafleur-pa-dagger-dig)

      * [T=2.8s] 3. The High-Low Conflict on the Mike: X drags across at 3 yards depth, fixing the Mike linebacker’s eyes underneath. Above Mike and below the pinned safeties, a massive 15-yard void forms in the center of the field.
      * [T=3.5s] 4. The 16-Yard Intermediate Dig Strike: Z snaps his 90-degree square-in right into the heart of the void. QB delivers a dart on the numbers for a first down and huge run-after-catch opportunity.

SCHEME FAMILY: NICK SIRIANNI'S POWER RPO & BROTHERLY SHOVE SYSTEM [ID: sirianni-power-rpo]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Architect / Coach: Nick Sirianni
Organization / Team: Philadelphia Eagles
Category: OFFENSE
Tree Branch: reid-west-coast
Core Philosophy: A physical, identity-driven offense built on gap power football paired with perimeter RPO access. Nick Sirianni's Eagles combine power duo runs that rely on vertical double-teams, RPO glance and slant reads that punish aggressive linebackers, boundary isolation for elite wide receivers, and the most famous short-yardage play in the NFL — the Brotherly Shove quarterback sneak.

PLAYS IN THIS SCHEME:

>>> PLAY: Inside Power Duo (Double Teams) (ID: sirianni-power-duo-inside)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: Gun 3x1 Trips Right, Offset RB Left
    Situation: 1st & 10, Own 40, base run down
    Defensive Look: Cover 2 Man (Nickel 4-2-5 Over Front)
    Animation Duration: 4s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=sirianni-power-rpo&play=sirianni-power-duo-inside

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Impose pure physical will at the line of scrimmage with interior Duo double teams, blowing defensive tackles off the ball and creating a heavy north-south running lane.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Mike Linebacker (Interior Gap Fitter)
    - Why It Works: Double-teaming both interior defensive linemen creates massive vertical displacement, leaving linebackers hesitant and easily climbed upon by guards.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A penetrating 3-technique DT splitting the RG/RT double-team before the combination can establish vertical push.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: sirianni-rpo-glance-iso, sirianni-slot-fade-out, sirianni-qb-sneak-push
    - Plays Off: None
    - Visual Tell Cue: Gun 3x1 formation with offensive line firing straight ahead on vertical power angles without pulling guards.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.8s] 1. The Dual Interior Double Teams: Philadelphia’s offensive line unleashes violent synchronized double teams: LG & C strike the 1-tech NT while RG & RT hammer the 3-tech DT, moving the defensive front backwards.
      * [T=1.8s] 2. Vertical Displacement of the Defensive Line: Both defensive tackles are blasted 2+ yards off the line of scrimmage, creating an impenetrable wall and swallowing up the interior gaps.
      * [T=2.6s] 3. The Second-Level Climb & Mike Collision: LG and RG seamlessly peel off their displaced defensive tackles to seal Mike and Will linebackers, opening a massive vertical crevice directly through the A-gap.
      * [T=3.6s] 4. Physical North-South Explosion: The running back hits the A-gap with high knees and north-south velocity, breaking through arm tackles for a punishing 9-yard gain.

>>> PLAY: Backside Glance ISO RPO (ID: sirianni-rpo-glance-iso)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: Gun 3x1 Trips Right, Solo X Left
    Situation: 2nd & 4, +42, RPO conflict call
    Defensive Look: Cover 3 Match (Apex Conflict) (Nickel 4-2-5 Over Front)

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]

    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Will Linebacker (Backside Conflict / Run-Fit LB)
    - Why It Works: The threat of Philadelphia’s interior double teams forces the Will LB to commit downhill into the B-gap; the isolated X receiver wins instantly on an inside slant with zero safety help.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Will linebacker freezing in the passing lane to bat the ball down or boundary cornerback jumping the slant inside with aggressive trap technique.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]

      * [T=1.4s] 2. The Will LB Sucked Into the Box: Stung by inside Duo on previous downs, the Will linebacker triggers downhill into the B-gap to stop the running back, completely vacating the intermediate slant window behind him.
      * [T=2.2s] 3. The Clean Pull & Glance Laser: QB snatches the ball out of the mesh, flips his hips, and fires a 12-yard dart to the isolated X receiver snapping inside on a physical 5-step Glance route.
      * [T=3.4s] 4. Physical Body Shield & YAC: X boxes out the boundary cornerback with his frame, secures the catch in stride between the numbers and hash, and rumbles forward for a 16-yard first down.

>>> PLAY: Slot Fade Out Isolation (ID: sirianni-slot-fade-out)
    Personnel: 11
    Formation: Gun 2x2 Doubles (Slot Left)
    Situation: 3rd & 6, +25, red zone fringe shot
    Defensive Look: Cover 1 Man (Nickel 4-2-5 Even Front)

    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Star / Nickel Defensive Back (Inside Leverage Slot Defender)
    - Why It Works: The inside stem threatens the nickelback’s inside leverage before snapping outside; the outside receiver’s quick out prevents the cornerback from sinking under the fade.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: Nickelback maintaining outside leverage off the line of scrimmage or Free Safety cheating over the slot fade instead of honoring the opposite post.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]

      * [T=1.6s] 2. The Rub & Out-Route Pin: Outside receiver X snaps on a 5-yard quick out to the boundary, occupying the left CB and clearing out the entire deep sideline corridor.
      * [T=2.4s] 3. The High-Arcing Fade Release: H bursts outside off his inside stem, stacking the nickelback along the boundary. QB drops a perfect high-trajectory rainbow toward the front pylon.
      * [T=3.5s] 4. Toe-Tap Touchdown in the Corner: H extends over his outside shoulder, snatches the ball over the trailing defender, and drags both feet cleanly in the back corner of the end zone for a 24-yard score.

>>> PLAY: Brotherly Shove (Tush Push) (ID: sirianni-qb-sneak-push)
    Personnel: 22 Jumbo
    Formation: Under Center Tight Wedge (Dual Pushers)
    Situation: 4th & 1, +1, goal line conversion
    Defensive Look: Goal Line 6-2 Man (Goal Line 6-2 Bear Front)
    Animation Duration: 3.5s
    Direct URL: https://schemedb.com/?scheme=sirianni-power-rpo&play=sirianni-qb-sneak-push

    [SUMMARY & TACTICAL PURPOSE]
    - Motive: Execute the mathematically and physically near-unstoppable short-yardage quarterback sneak by combining low offensive line pad leverage with dual backfield pushers.
    - Key Defender Put In Conflict: Nose Tackles & Mike Linebacker (Interior Goal-Line Squeeze)
    - Why It Works: The Center and Guards create a low-to-high wedge underneath the defensive line, while dual pushers deliver immediate secondary kinetic thrust before the defense can halt forward progress.
    - Failure Mode / Defensive Counter: A false start / offsides penalty or defensive nose tackles timing the snap and cutting the center’s legs from underneath before the pushers engage.

    [SEQUENCING & GAME-PLAN LOGIC]
    - Sets Up: None
    - Plays Off: sirianni-power-duo-inside, sirianni-slot-fade-out
    - Visual Tell Cue: Ultra-tight wedge splits along the offensive line with dual pushers aligned directly behind the quarterback’s hips.

    [TIMELINE COACHING BEATS]
      * [T=0.5s] 1. Subterranean Pad Level at the Snap: Philadelphia’s center and guards fire out with near-zero pad level, wedging their helmets beneath the breastplates of the goal-line nose tackles to create immediate underneath leverage.
      * [T=1.2s] 2. The Direct A-Gap Insertion: The quarterback takes the snap and dives instantly into the low crevice created by the Center, keeping his center of gravity below the defensive line’s knees.
      * [T=1.8s] 3. Dual-Pusher Kinetic Thrust: Both flanking pushers (P1 and P2) latch firmly onto the quarterback’s hips, followed by the fullback, creating an overwhelming 600+ pound wall of forward kinetic force.
      * [T=3.0s] 4. The Inevitable Conversion: Even with linebackers leaping over the pile, the sheer horizontal power of the wedge drives the entire defensive front 2 yards backwards across the goal line for a guaranteed conversion.
